subject: arts-music
unit_title: Sharing My Work: Portfolio and Choice Showcase
lesson_title: Synthesis and review: giving and receiving feedback

rubric.exceeds: All required evidence for giving and receiving feedback is present, clearly labelled, and includes the required work blocks and one reviewable process state plus a complete criteria check.
rubric.meets: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
rubric.developing: The central Arts work is present, but one required evidence part for giving and receiving feedback is missing or cannot be located.
rubric.beginning: The submission does not yet contain the central cross-modal arts practice evidence required by this lesson.

rubric.exceeds: The learner precisely locates sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, explains how multiple relationships work together, and identifies a meaningful tradeoff.
rubric.meets: The learner locates relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
rubric.developing: Relevant choices are attempted, but the explanation does not yet locate their effect or connect it consistently with the stated purpose.
rubric.beginning: The work does not yet provide locatable evidence of giving and receiving feedback; use the registered retry route without judging style or ability.

rubric.exceeds: The reasoning supports the learner’s choices, recognizes another defensible route, and distinguishes objective constraints from open artistic decisions.
rubric.meets: The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
rubric.developing: An intent or interpretation is stated, but key claims rely on preference, polish, or resemblance rather than evidence.
rubric.beginning: No supported intent or interpretation is visible yet; no particular style, mood, subject, or model-like result is required.

rubric.exceeds: Earlier and later evidence makes the tested relationship traceable; the learner gives a criteria-based reason to revise or deliberately keep the result.
rubric.meets: The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.
rubric.developing: A change is visible, but the evidence that prompted it or the relationship changed is unclear.
rubric.beginning: No check or revision decision is visible yet; invite a bounded test without directing the learner’s artistic choice.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score giving and receiving feedback with the focus-facing rubric, not a fixed answer key. Record objective presence first. For judgment-based dimensions, cite locatable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent from the actual submission and connect it to the learner’s intent or claim. Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Difference from an Academy model is never an error and resemblance earns no extra credit. A learner may revise the work, revise the stated intention, support ambiguity, or keep the result when the evidence-based reasoning is coherent. A rough or model-different result can meet the lesson when the evidence and reasoning satisfy the criterion. Never infer talent, taste, effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from the work.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about giving and receiving feedback.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about giving and receiving feedback; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: There is no fixed composition or answer for giving and receiving feedback. Score the authored objective constraints and the focus-specific rubric evidence; accept materially different creative, performance, design, or interpretive choices when the learner supports them against the criteria.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique, revision, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence/reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Route 1: Reduce giving and receiving feedback to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension_plan: Apply giving and receiving feedback under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on giving and receiving feedback rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.

safety_and_privacy.note: No public performance, camera, voice recording, photograph, or audience is required at any point; a private option and a written/no-audio alternative are stated in the task package and score identically.
